item.title: 2026 Fall Fitness Prescription: Bridging Clinical Science and Practice
item.description:
As an Adjunct Lecturer in the Department of Leisure and Recreation Management at Taipei City University of Science and Technology, I focus on transforming a passion for fitness into a scientifically grounded, clinical career. My teaching methodology bridges the gap between exercise physiology and real-world application.

Foundational Science, Clinical Assessment, Evidence-Based Prescription!

2026 Fall Fitness Prescription

Bridging the Gap Between Science and Application

In my course, 2026 Fall Fitness Prescription, I guide students through the industry’s highest clinical standards—the ACSM’s Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription. My approach ensures that future professionals don’t just memorize protocols but deeply understand the physiological mechanisms driving clinical and athletic adaptations. By integrating English as a Medium of Instruction (EMI) methodologies, the course utilizes active learning strategies like Think-Pair-Share and scaffolding to ensure complex concepts remain highly accessible.

This instructional framework prepares students for advanced practice and certifications such as the ACSM-EP and ACSM-CEP, focusing on risk stratification, cardiometabolic assessments, and exercise medicine.

Watch Course Description on YouTube

Core Pillars of My Instruction

The curriculum is built around three critical domains:

  1. Foundational Physiology & Assessment: We explore bioenergetics, cardiopulmonary physiology, and movement science. It’s not just about knowing the energy systems; it’s about utilizing tools like heart rate monitoring and muscle oxygenation concepts to understand how the human body responds to stress.
  2. Evidence-Based Prescription: From aerobic interval training to advanced resistance training, students learn to apply the FITT-VP principle (Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type, Volume, Progression) accurately for diverse populations.
  3. Clinical & Special Populations: This is where science meets healthcare. Students learn to design safe, effective programs for individuals with metabolic concerns, cardiovascular conditions, and aging populations, utilizing functional strength equipment appropriately to build capacity.

Inside the Classroom: Practical Teaching Demonstrations

Translating Movement Science to Client Success

A proficient exercise physiologist must be able to analyze movement mechanics instantly. In this segment, I explain how to assess biomechanics across all planes of motion and apply these findings to clinical exercise prescription, reducing injury risk and maximizing functional outcomes.

Watch on YouTube

Mastering the Initial Consultation and Risk Stratification

Success in fitness prescription begins with thorough screening. This video captures how I teach students to conduct a comprehensive health history interview, perform risk stratification, and establish the foundational framework for targeted aerobic and resistance training routines.

Watch on YouTube

Long-Term Programming Strategy: Manipulating FITT-VP

To prevent client plateaus and manage chronic conditions, professionals must master periodization. Here, I illustrate how to strategically manipulate FITT-VP variables to create sustainable, long-term physiological adaptations, ensuring safe progression for all fitness levels.

Watch on YouTube

The Golden Rules of Physiological Adaptation

Generic workouts fail to produce specific clinical or performance results. In this lecture highlight, I break down the core principles of training: Specificity, Overload, and Progression. I emphasize aligning energy systems and functional movements with a client’s unique health markers—a critical competency in the field of exercise prescription.

Watch on YouTube

Professional Excellence & Certification

The ultimate goal of this methodology is to ensure students are ready to pass rigorous professional examinations and lead clients toward better health outcomes with absolute confidence.

  • Instructional Focus: Meticulously aligned with ACSM-EP and ACSM-CEP competencies.
  • Pedagogical Innovation: Integration of EMI active learning strategies and functional training principles.
  • Industry Expertise: Grounded in my experience as a PhD candidate and holder of ACSM-CEP, ACSM-EP, and NSCA-CSCS*D certifications.

item.title: 2026 Functional Exercise Activity Design: Bridging Movement Science and Practice
item.description:
As an Adjunct Lecturer in the Department of Leisure and Recreation Management at Taipei City University of Science and Technology, I focus on transforming a passion for fitness into a scientifically grounded career. My teaching methodology bridges the gap between movement science and real-world functional application.

Foundational Movement, Functional Equipment, Activity Design!

2026 Functional Exercise Activity Design

Bridging the Gap Between Science and Application

In my course, 2026 Functional Exercise Activity Design, I guide students through the principles of functional movement, drawing inspiration from high-performance protocols like HYROX and the NSCA’s Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning. By integrating English as a Medium of Instruction (EMI) methodologies and active learning strategies like Think-Pair-Share and scaffolding, my approach ensures that future professionals don’t just memorize terms but deeply understand the biomechanics of multi-planar movement.

This instructional framework prepares students for advanced practice and coaching certifications, focusing on movement efficiency, velocity-based training, and the practical application of functional strength equipment.

Watch Course Description on YouTube

Core Pillars of My Instruction

The curriculum is built around three critical domains:

  1. Foundational Movement Science: We explore kinetic chains, bioenergetics, and biomechanics. It’s not just about naming muscles; it’s about understanding how the human body generates power across the sagittal, frontal, and transverse planes during dynamic, real-world activities.
  2. Applied Functional Technique: From kettlebell swings and free weights to velocity-based training and cardiovascular intervals, students utilize a wide array of functional implements to refine their coaching and demonstration skills.
  3. Activity Design & Programming: This is where science becomes art. Students learn to design safe, effective functional programs for diverse goals—from strength-endurance to high-intensity functional training—and for populations ranging from athletic competitors to those seeking improved daily mobility.

Inside the Classroom: Practical Teaching Demonstrations

Translating Movement Science to Client Success

A proficient strength and conditioning coach must be able to analyze a client’s foundational movement patterns—such as the hinge, squat, push, pull, and carry—instantly. In this segment, I explain how to assess movement efficiency using functional tools like free weights. By deeply understanding kinetic linking, future instructors can provide precise verbal cues and drastically reduce the risk of client injury.

Watch on YouTube

Mastering the Functional Assessment and Framework

Success in functional training relies on identifying movement limitations and properly introducing equipment. This video captures how I teach students to conduct dynamic movement assessments and establish the foundational framework for safely integrating kettlebells and velocity-based metrics into a client’s routine.

Watch on YouTube

Long-Term Programming Strategy: Manipulating Variables for Functional Fitness

To prevent client plateaus and overtraining, professionals must master the art of periodization for functional fitness. Here, I illustrate how to strategically manipulate FITT-VP variables specifically for functional and HYROX-style conditioning, ensuring sustainable, long-term adaptations.

Watch on YouTube

The Golden Rules of Functional Adaptation

Generic workouts fail to produce movement proficiency. In this lecture highlight, I break down the core principles of functional training: Specificity, Overload, and Movement Quality. I place a strong emphasis on aligning energy systems and functional mechanics with a client’s unique health or performance goals.

Watch on YouTube

Professional Excellence & Certification

The ultimate goal of this methodology is to ensure students are ready to lead clients toward their functional goals with absolute confidence and scientific backing.

  • Instructional Focus: Meticulously aligned with NSCA-CSCS domains and advanced functional training standards.
  • Pedagogical Innovation: Integration of EMI active learning strategies and hands-on application with functional strength equipment.
  • Industry Expertise: Grounded in my experience as a PhD candidate and holder of NSCA-CSCS*D, ACSM-CEP, and ACSM-EP certifications.

item.title: 2025 Spring Fitness Instructor Teaching Methodology: Bridging Science and Practice
item.description:
As an Adjunct Lecturer in the Department of Leisure and Recreation Management at Taipei City University of Science and Technology, I focus on transforming a passion for fitness into a scientifically grounded career. My teaching methodology bridges the gap between exercise science and real-world application.

Foundational Science, Applied Technique, Program Design!

Fitness Instructor Teaching Methodology

Bridging the Gap Between Science and Application

In my course, Fitness Instructor Teaching Methodology, I guide students through the “Gold Standard” of the industry—the NSCA’s Essentials of Personal Training. My approach ensures that future professionals don’t just memorize terms but understand the “why” behind the “how.”

This instructional video provides an overview of how the course is structured to prepare students for the NSCA-CPT certification, focusing on anatomical adaptations, biomechanics, and the legal responsibilities of a fitness professional.

Watch Course Description on YouTube

Core Pillars of My Instruction

Based on my teaching demonstration, the curriculum is built around three critical domains:

  1. Foundational Science: We explore anatomy, bioenergetics, and biomechanics. It’s not just about naming muscles; it’s about understanding how the human body generates power and adapts to stress.
  2. Applied Technique: From stability exercises to advanced resistance training and cardiovascular protocols, students utilize hundreds of techniques outlined in the textbook and online resources to refine their coaching skills.
  3. Program Design: This is where science becomes art. Students learn to design safe, effective programs for diverse goals—from hypertrophy to aerobic endurance—and for Special Populations, including those with metabolic concerns, cardiovascular conditions, or spinal cord injuries.

Inside the Classroom: Practical Teaching Demonstrations

Translating Movement Science to Client Success

A proficient personal trainer must be able to analyze a client’s posture and movement efficiency instantly. In this segment, I explain how to utilize the three planes of motion (sagittal, frontal, and transverse) and varying lever systems in practical scenarios. By deeply understanding concentric, eccentric, and isometric contractions, future fitness instructors can provide precise verbal cues and drastically reduce the risk of client injury.

Watch on YouTube

Mastering the Initial Consultation and Program Framework

Success in personal training relies as much on interpersonal communication as it does on exercise prescription. This video captures how I teach students to bridge these two skills. I demonstrate how to professionally introduce yourself to a new client while simultaneously establishing the foundational framework for both their aerobic and resistance training routines.

Watch on YouTube

Long-Term Programming Strategy: The GAS Model

To prevent client plateaus and overtraining, fitness professionals must master the art of periodization. Here, I introduce the General Adaptation Syndrome (GAS) to illustrate how the human body responds to physiological stress. Students learn to strategically manipulate FITT-VP variables (Frequency, Intensity, Time, Type, Volume, Progression) to create sustainable, long-term adaptations for their clients.

Watch on YouTube

The Golden Rules of Physiological Adaptation

Generic workouts fail to produce specific results. In this lecture highlight, I break down the three non-negotiable rules of training: Specificity, Overload, and Progression. I place a strong emphasis on the Principle of Specificity, teaching students how to select exercises and energy systems that directly align with a client’s unique health or performance goals—a critical competency tested in the NSCA-CPT exam.

Watch on YouTube

Professional Excellence & Certification

The ultimate goal of this methodology is to ensure students are ready to pass professional examinations and lead clients toward their goals with absolute confidence.

  • Instructional Focus: Meticulously aligned with NSCA-CPT exam domains.
  • Practical Skills: Emphasizing business ethics and legal responsibilities to ensure career success.
  • Industry Expertise: Grounded in my experience as a PhD candidate and holder of NSCA-CSCS*D and ACSM-CEP certifications.

item.title: 2025 Spring Weight Training Instruction Methodology: Bridging Science and Practice
item.description:
As an Adjunct Lecturer in the Department of Leisure and Recreation Management at Taipei City University of Science and Technology, I focus on transforming a passion for strength training into a scientifically grounded career. My teaching methodology bridges the gap between exercise science and practical weight training application.

Foundational Science, Applied Technique, Program Design!

Weight Training Instruction Methodology

Bridging the Gap Between Science and Application

In my course, Weight Training Instruction Methodology, I guide students through the essential principles of resistance training as outlined in the NSCA’s Essentials of Personal Training. My approach ensures that future professionals understand not only “how” to train clients but also “why” these methods are effective.

This instructional video provides an overview of how the course is structured to prepare students for NSCA-CPT certification, emphasizing muscular adaptations, biomechanics of lifts, and the safety and legal responsibilities of a fitness professional.

Watch Course Description on YouTube

Core Pillars of My Instruction

The curriculum is built around three critical domains specifically for weight training:

  1. Foundational Science: Students explore anatomy, muscle physiology, and biomechanics. Beyond identifying muscles, they learn how force is generated, how muscles adapt to resistance, and the science behind progressive overload.

  2. Applied Technique: From fundamental lifts like squats, deadlifts, and presses to advanced accessory exercises, students practice proper form, spotting, and coaching techniques to ensure safety and effectiveness.

  3. Program Design: This is where science becomes art. Students learn to create individualized strength programs for diverse goals—from hypertrophy to maximal strength—and for Special Populations, including those with orthopedic limitations, metabolic concerns, or post-injury rehabilitation needs.

Interactive Course Demonstrations

Applied Anatomy and Biomechanics

To build a solid foundation, students must understand the mechanics behind every movement. In this session, we dive into applied anatomy and biomechanics, covering the three primary planes of motion (sagittal, transverse, and frontal), the different classes of levers, and the three distinct types of muscle contractions (eccentric, concentric, and isometric). This scientific grounding is essential for safe and effective personal training.

Watch on YouTube

Training Principles and Program Design

Leisure and sports are not just about fun; they are deeply rooted in science. This module introduces core exercise principles, emphasizing the progression of training. Students learn how to apply these concepts to design individualized resistance and aerobic exercise programs. We also cover practical professional skills, such as how to confidently introduce yourself to clients and guide them toward a better, scientifically-backed workout.

Watch on YouTube

Periodization Training and General Adaptation Syndrome (GAS)

Developing an effective long-term program requires an understanding of periodization. By exploring the General Adaptation Syndrome (GAS), students learn how the body adapts to stress. I explain how to manipulate critical training variables—frequency, intensity, type, time, and volume—to match individual adaptations, ensuring optimal progression and setting the stage for a successful fitness coaching career.

Watch on YouTube

Core Principles of Training: Specificity, Overload, and Progression

When instructing exercise technique and spotting, applying the right theoretical framework is vital. In this segment, I detail the three main pillars of training: Specificity, Overload, and Progression. I specifically highlight the Principle of Specificity, illustrating how targeted movements and exercise routines must be carefully selected to achieve the exact physiological adaptations your clients desire.

Watch on YouTube

Professional Excellence & Certification

The ultimate goal of this methodology is to ensure students are fully prepared to pass professional certification exams and lead clients toward their strength goals safely and effectively.

  • Instructional Focus: Aligned with NSCA-CPT exam domains, emphasizing resistance training principles.
  • Practical Skills: Covering coaching cues, injury prevention, and legal responsibilities for professional practice.
  • Industry Expertise: Grounded in my experience as a PhD candidate and holder of NSCA-CSCS*D and ACSM-CEP certifications.
